column4: The known lower construction must be paired with a sharp universal upper bound 3q^2+q+1, q=2m+n; the source upper bound is about 9q^2. Controlling colored special two-paths in arbitrary planar embeddings, rather than finding one large clique, is the missing mechanism. Source records (1,0) and (0,2) as known cases.

A union bound for low-weight sums of check rows would need probability estimates after conditioning simultaneously on both regularity and logarithmic girth. Independent check sampling does not survive that conditioning. Every constant c and the diverging weight threshold must be handled.

Raynaud surfaces attain the proposed ratio; the absent half is a universal inequality for all minimal general-type surfaces, not just the smallest-genus quasi-hyperelliptic part. The computed p=5 case gives no full-prime certificate.

column2: Conjecture III.1 and immediately following paragraph
column4: The primary body immediately says the conjecture does not hold; maximizing the displayed symbol-extension formula cannot prove optimality over practical precoding systems. Even the displayed 1.4998 is rounded. This is an existing source retraction, not a fresh counterexample.

A universal locating-dominating set of size at most floor(n/2) would yield the eventual maximum with the existing lower examples. Cubic/twin-free special cases in the paper do not provide the arbitrary-degree selection argument; small enumeration cannot settle eventual equality.

The proposed route embeds a spanning planar triangulation through the Z_l framework and Lemma 7.2; a degree-sequence host embedding theorem with slack eta is still required. One dense graph or a finite n search cannot control every eta and its asymptotic threshold.

The literal record suppresses the piecewise restricted triple-sum bound in Theorem 14. A viable check must implement that exact bound including congruence exceptions and enumerate restricted threefold sumsets, not ordinary sumsets or only critical numbers. The theorem formula and dependency proof were not fully audited here.

A dynamic-programming minimax certificate on one weighted cycle could refute the bound, but all positive weight vectors and both optimal move choices need a strategy inequality for a proof. The weighted-tree bound cannot simply be transferred because deleting an edge changes available play.

The lower bound is already public. The only creditable positive mechanism would be n(p-1) explicit p-phase vectors covering every word under the complex bilinear dot product, uniformly for all p dividing n. Covering a few small cubes or switching to a Hermitian convention does not supply it.

Rayleigh vectors split at a centroid give coarse O(1/n) control; the sharp d(d-2)/(d-1) coefficient requires balanced-branch spectral comparison with a uniform logarithmic error. A finite exceptional tree cannot refute an asymptotic big-O statement without a family.

A candidate counterexample needs certified inequalities for normalized entries of exp(A) and their arccos averages, not adjacency spectral radius alone. Exact primary angle definitions and a complete interval arithmetic comparison were not audited; numerical graph rankings are not proof.

Euler characteristic and an insertion construction might realize every target region count, but must maintain pairwise intersection while controlling simultaneous intersections and tangencies. Generic perturbation creates jumps of two; proving that every missing parity is attainable is the unresolved construction step. Small-n wording is no credit.

For a fixed cut Chernoff control is easy; the assertion quantifies over every maximizing cut and every vertex in the sparse logarithmic regime. A switching argument must beat dependence on the optimizing cut; union bounding all cuts loses the desired threshold.

Rayleigh domain monotonicity orders nested Dirichlet sets but not singleton boundary sides of different lengths. A triangle-wide transplantation or reflection inequality would be needed; numerical PDE eigenvalues on samples cannot certify all shapes. Inherited triangle-gap routes remain parked.

Minimal Ramsey graphs for K_k are not automatically minimal for K_(k-1); trimming can reduce degrees. The source relates the parameter to colored packing and Erdos-Rogers functions, so a monotone extremal reduction is needed beyond inclusion of Ramsey properties.

An optimal ranking with each specified vertex uniquely labeled 1 would need a minor-critical structural argument. Reranking one familiar family only repeats the paper's examples; criticality alone does not give a direct reranking move at an arbitrary vertex.

A full proof requires eventual separation of every pair of squarefree-level newforms by the first prime away from the level, uniformly in large weights for each level. Finite Hecke tables and Sturm bounds at a fixed weight do not establish that eventual single-prime simplicity.

A rational generating function or finite-state Ehrhart description could produce residue-class limits, but no such complete encoding for every genus is established here. The unknown period and positivity in every residue prevent numerical cluster plots from being decisive.

column2: Conjecture 1; Theorem 2 proof and cube example
column4: The source proves that regular 2-swappable graphs with one edge-card type have edge reconstruction number at least three, then exhibits the standard cube. Repeating that blocker mechanism is a public refutation, irrespective of the stale open label.

For three longest paths, one must turn the t_P=2 transition structure into a common vertex by path rerouting. Pairwise intersections are insufficient, and an improvement to a positive distance bound does not prove f=0. Exact transition definitions require further dependency audit.

A proof must establish both global maximality and uniqueness of the carousel limit homomorphism for every odd size at least five. A finite flag-algebra certificate for one size would be an instance; a uniform equality-case argument is missing.

column2: Conjecture 2; Kemnitz discussion; threshold closing remarks
column4: The displayed all-k formula is already contradicted by the neighboring Kemnitz setting: C_2^2 with k=1 predicts length 4 but four distinct elements have no zero-sum pair. This diagnoses an omitted threshold, not an eligible new result. The quoted solved status concerns Kemnitz, not the general threshold program.

A counterexample needs finite congruence coverings for every identical outer digit and all repetition lengths, with n not divisible by 3 or in the excluded 11 class. Searching for no prime up to a cutoff cannot prove a(n)=0; the source's 231 example is already public and divisible by 3.

The forward last-digit obstruction is elementary and known. The hard direction requires a prime in at least one of nine exponential repunit-prefix sequences for every allowed n; Dirichlet's theorem on unrestricted arithmetic progressions does not apply to this sparse set. No complete covering counterexample was obtained.

A certificate must cover arbitrary edge-list assignments with lists of size chi-prime. The bipartite and bounded tree-width results are public restrictions, not a solution for general graphs; asymptotic slack cannot be removed by finite checking.

A possible induction would compare the Perron root of successive radix-a bricklayer blocks to (a-1)log_a(n), controlling off-diagonal couplings and equality only at powers. The binary proof and Hamming-ball discussion do not supply that induction; exact block definitions and dependencies remain unaudited.

The proposed disjoint K_k,k family supplies 2^(n/(2k)) choices. A proof needs a multiplicative upper bound for all k-dominating independent-set families. A denser component with a larger per-vertex count could refute it, but no exact component certificate was constructed; the k=2 exception is not the target k>3.

column2: Conjecture 1; symmetry Property 4 and Proposition discussion
column4: Reciprocity gives a stationary point at rho_V=1, not uniqueness or a minimum. Implicit differentiation of the normalization equation for rho_R could prove a sign rule for P_b prime, but denominators and global positive solution uniqueness need audit for every capacity and traffic ratio. No derivative certificate executed.

Matroid-union rank integration or a random graph process limit could prove convergence at each fixed k. The paper's k-to-infinity ratio bound does not identify equal n-liminf/limsup for each k; finite simulations or concentration alone do not close that limit interchange.

The quantifier ranges over all covering maxima in every dimension at least six. Enumeration of perfect Delaunay polytopes in a few dimensions cannot exclude competing maxima in unbounded dimensions; full reduction/classification would be a deep program rather than a small certificate.

The cited body is a survey rather than the originating Cao-Dehmer-Schaumann article. Any entropy counterexample must first bind its actual information function and original exponent domain. Degree smoothing or majorization for a different entropy would not settle this target; no primary-origin or successor clearance was performed.

The source explicitly says Theorem 1.1 implies the pair-version conjecture because arboricity and degeneracy differ by at most a factor two. Proving the pair statement from the degenerate Ramsey theorem is a public corollary, not discovery credit.

Concavity would follow from an appropriate coupling controlling speed increments as drift varies, but monotonicity of individual walks does not imply concavity of the interacting front. Stationary-law heuristics require existence and differentiated control over the full parameter interval.

Symmetrizing hole labels is legitimate but does not force a fixed pair of depths independent of same-hole placement. An extremal measure reduction must preserve payoff against every adaptive search strategy for every n,h; a finite discretized linear program is not the continuous game.

column4: The primary source expressly says the minimum-rank terminal-word version is still open and Kari refuted the stronger arbitrary attainable-rank claim. A Kari automaton cannot be assumed to refute this formulation. The target contains the synchronizing rank-one bound, so no small uniform route is supported.

Definitions of triangle packing t_e and partition admissibility must be audited before a small-graph certificate; no enumeration executed.

column4: The source itself notes disjoint one-edge ordinary graphs have equal Laplacian/signless radii 2 in every power, violating strict decrease, and proves decrease after excluding those objects. Both the exception and corrected theorem are public; neither merits new credit.

A 53rd planar critical P7-free graph with explicit coloring/minimality and embedding certificates could refute completeness. Searches through order 30 cannot prove no larger graph exists; a structural upper order bound is needed for a positive result. No new graph or exhaustive search produced.

The two-parameter family's spectral radius admits a quotient formula, but the missing universal step bounds TErr for every tree degree sequence. Optimizing the a,b formula alone proves only the proposed comparison family's envelope and does not establish domination over all BFS trees.

Dobrowolski and McKee concern nonrepresentable totally real integers, not directly the asymptotic graph multiplicity inequality. Nonrepresentability invalidates one construction route rather than proving an asymptotic gap. A general graph construction or uniform upper-gap obstruction is still needed.

column4: Arbitrary real lists must produce a proper total coloring with distinct neighboring weighted degrees and asymptotic coefficient one. The paper explicitly says its ordinary-coloring approaches do not extend, even the Kahn-based approach; a new list-preserving probabilistic/resampling mechanism is absent.

column4: The source states that the Yin partition already contains every simultaneous bar-core, then asks for one containing every even bar-core without explicitly requiring the containing partition to be even. The literal claim is a subset corollary of the preceding known result. Inferring an even-containing version would change the target and requires separate primary clarification, not credit here.

Beta concerns a positive fraction of field values rather than surjectivity. The universal even-dimensional half-dimension threshold needs energy/exponential-sum control for arbitrary sets and all k, with constants correctly uniform in q. A two-resultant result or one family of sets is insufficient.

The source prints G1=4K3 and G2=K5 plus seven isolated vertices at n=12. Their packing would put five pairwise nonadjacent G1 vertices into K5, impossible since alpha(4K3)=4; edge/degree total 26 is below 3n-7=29. A finite-exceptions amendment is a different claim.

Finitely many zero terms require a representation for all sufficiently large primes, not a bound on k conditional on representability. The displayed logarithmic bound in Proposition 4 does not eliminate the zero case. Covering primes with the source arithmetic progressions would need an eventual covering proof.

column2: Conjecture 3.2 and final on-line list-edge-coloring discussion
column4: The t=0 specialization is the on-line list edge-coloring problem. A scheduling proof for positive absences cannot bypass that endpoint; known special complete/bipartite cases and the Shannon-type upper bound do not yield chi-prime+2t for every multigraph.

Decomposing dense graphs into disjoint minor-bearing subgraphs loses the sharp additive constant; confirming single cycles or a few multiplicities cannot close the all-pattern assertion.

Covering all edges of every r-graph with 2r-1 perfect matchings is equivalent to the generalized Berge-Fulkerson program; fractional matching decompositions do not automatically select a small integral cover. The cubic five-cover case alone is already a major unresolved component in the source.

The reported solved quote is about maximal weakly separated sets, a different earlier conjecture. Source proves the target for t=2,3, k=2 and one sortedness condition, leaving general cubical distances. A full proof needs a uniform minor-order inequality beyond those public cases.

A derivative bound on theta+lambda*h(v)-v for its Gaussian expectation could prove uniqueness, but the equal-cluster concavity lemma cannot be assumed for unequal clusters; exact domain and recursion dependency audit is pending.
